title: Orzo With Spinach and Feta
description: By Melissa Clark: Similar to spanakorizo, a Greek spinach and rice dish, this easy, meatless meal features orzo, spinach, peas and scallions. It is deeply satisfying but still on the lighter side of pasta recipes, thanks to all those vegetables. A little feta gives it creaminess and tang, while some lemon zest brightens everything up. It makes a complete meal on its own, or, if you’re looking for something more substantial, serve this as a hearty side dish to roasted meats or fish.
ingredients: 4 large scallions, trimmed and thinly sliced
8 ounces baby spinach leaves (8 cups), coarsely chopped
1¾ cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable stock
1 teaspoon finely grated lemon zest (from 1 lemon)
¾ cup crumbled feta (3 ounces), plus more for garnish
1 cup chopped fresh dill, or use parsley or cilantro
directions: Heat a 10-inch skillet over medium, then melt butter, 30 seconds to 1 minute. Stir in about three-quarters of the scallions (saving some of the green parts for garnish) and garlic, and cook until softened, stirring frequently, about 3 minutes.

Stir in stock and bring to a simmer. Stir in orzo, lemon zest and remaining ½ teaspoon salt. Cover and simmer over medium-low heat until orzo is nearly cooked through and most of the liquid is absorbed, 10 minutes or so for al dente, stirring once or twice.

Stir in spinach, adding in batches if it doesn’t all fit in the pan at once, and ½ teaspoon salt. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until spinach is wilted, and the orzo is fully cooked, a minute or two.
Stir in cheese, peas (if you like) and dill, cover the pan, and cook for another 1 minute, to finish cooking and warm the peas. To serve, sprinkle with more cheese and the reserved scallions.
